In ancient history, what was Japan before it was a Shogunate?

So right before the Shogunate was "established" was the Heian Period of Japanese culture (I don't really like to use words like that because history is super fluid and people don't move from one distinct life-mode to the next, things change gradually over time) which generally took place between 794-1185 CE, ending with the Genpei war and the establishment of Minamoto's shogunate based out of Kamakura.

So the Heian Period was one in which many modern aspects of Japanese culture begin to emerge, and to outsiders like us this is the period in which the peoples of Honshu island really begin to become "Japanese". This was a time of high art and culture and the country was ruled over by an emperor. This was also when Buddhism began to move into Japan from China, specifically Pure Land Buddhism, whose doctrine is an awful lot like Protestantism.

Check out more about the Heian Period here and let me know if you have anymore questions.

So, basically, the very broad and big picture of Japan's history (starting with the Heian period) begins with an empire, then the shogunate, back to an empire where the emperor holds most if not all the power, to today's UK-esque government where Japan's emperor, like the UK's monarch, is more of a figurehead/ceremonial formality (I briefly skimmed Wikipedia), where a parliament does a lot of decision making?
I can't speak to the contemporary history of Japan, but yes: Proto-tribes, tribes, Kingdoms, Empire, Shogunate to whatever they are now.
